description.value: The World's Largest Paddle is a Guinness World Records-certified roadside attraction near Golden, BC — a locally crafted Western Red Cedar and LVL paddle scaled 13 times to over 60 feet, set against the backdrop of the Canadian Rockies and Columbia River Valley. Adjacent to the paddle is the Columbia Wetlands Outpost, where visitors can rent canoes, kayaks, SUPs, and pedal boats, or join a guided cataraft float through wetlands home to over 350 wildlife species. Located on Hwy 95 about 26 km south of Golden, it is a natural stop for cyclists touring the Columbia River corridor.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully fetched and describes a Guinness World Record roadside attraction near Golden, BC — a 60-foot cedar paddle on Hwy 95 with an adjacent Columbia Wetlands Outpost offering boat rentals and guided tours. The site mentions dock furniture, a nature walk, suspension bridge, and riverfront access, but contains no references to bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or any cycling-specific amenities. OSM has no phone or address; the website supplies a toll-free phone number. The website URL matches the OSM-provided URL.
